title: Respiratory Deterioration Simulation
description: Timed simulation focused on identifying and escalating worsening respiratory status.

questions.prompt: Which findings require immediate follow-up? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: SpO2 of 88% indicates hypoxemia requiring immediate intervention. A respiratory rate of 30/min reflects significant respiratory distress and compensatory work of breathing. Bilateral basilar crackles suggest fluid accumulation (pulmonary edema) or atelectasis and are clinically significant. A request for a warm blanket is a comfort need and not a clinical emergency.
questions.rationale: Rapid recognition of deteriorating respiratory status is a high-stakes nursing competency. The combination of low SpO2, tachypnea, and abnormal lung sounds forms a pattern consistent with acute respiratory compromise requiring immediate assessment and provider notification.

distractorRationale.D: A request for a warm blanket is a routine comfort need. While nurses should address it, it does not represent a clinical finding requiring urgent follow-up compared to the objective signs of respiratory compromise described in the other options.

questions.prompt: What is the priority nursing action?

choices.text: Raise the head of the bed and apply oxygen per protocol.
Delay action until the provider rounds.
Document findings and reassess in one hour.

questions.explanation: Elevating the head of the bed to high-Fowler's position reduces the work of breathing by allowing the diaphragm to descend and improves ventilation-perfusion matching. Applying supplemental oxygen directly addresses hypoxemia. These are the two immediate nurse-initiated actions before provider notification for a client in respiratory distress.
questions.rationale: Positioning and oxygenation are within nursing scope and should not be delayed. This question tests the learner's ability to prioritize nurse-initiated actions that improve oxygenation immediately versus delegating decision-making to the provider or deferring care.

distractorRationale.B: Delaying action in a client with SpO2 of 88%, RR of 30, and crackles is unsafe. Nurses have the authority and obligation to initiate evidence-based interventions and notify the provider urgently without waiting for rounds.
distractorRationale.C: Encouraging oral fluids is inappropriate when the client has bilateral crackles suggesting pulmonary fluid accumulation; increasing oral intake could worsen the respiratory status.
distractorRationale.D: Documenting without acting is never appropriate for an acute deterioration. Documentation follows intervention, not the reverse.
